narr: An unstable warm sector with MUCAPE up to 2000-2500 J/kg developed during the afternoon between an advancing cold front across southeast South Dakota and a gangly warm front extending into southwest Minnesota. An approaching weak impulse spurred rapid development of multiple rounds of storms near the warm front, initially discrete, with upscale growth into short bowing segments. Secondary development occurred during the evening along the cold front, which evolved into a slow-moving linear system with hail, wind, and heavy rainfall with shear vectors increasingly parallel to the boundary.
ev: Significant street flooding continued along Heritage Parkway and 271st Street.

As a response to 3 to 5 inches of rainfall across the southern portions of Sioux Falls, the Big Sioux at Western Avenue (gage site WAVS2) climbed into flood stage at 2130CST, with a crest 0.94 feet above flood stage at 2230CST. The Sioux Falls Marathon, which was scheduled to begin at 0530CST, was cancelled due to the overnight flash flooding.
Numerous roads in Tea were under water. Significant flooding with up to 2 feet of water was reported on portions of 271st Street and Heritage Parkway.
The roadway of 6th Street and Cliff Avenue was estimated to around a foot deep.
Water pooled up to two feet deep in the backyard of an apartment complex near 41st Street and South Dakota Highway 11.
Ponding of water caused water to reach basements.
Significant ponding of water resulted in some basement flooding.
Significant ponding and flooding of a small creek resulted in some basement flooding in lower spots.
